note.question: When should a UGC platform adopt affiliate marketing, how should it split commissions with creators, and how does the model affect content quality, consumer welfare, and affiliated and nonaffiliated creators?
note.overview: Affiliate marketing is modeled as a three-stage game in which the UGC platform commits to a commission-split rate, competing affiliated and nonaffiliated creators choose production effort, and consumers allocate attention. The authors derive the subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium by backward induction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: With affiliate marketing, stage 0 has the platform announce commission-split rate alpha. In stage 1, affiliated and nonaffiliated creators simultaneously choose production efforts. In stage 2, consumers observe resulting content quality, allocate consumption time across creators, and may purchase through affiliate links.
